# discover_repos { #crossrepo.gitutil.discover_repos }

```python
crossrepo.gitutil.discover_repos(roots)
```

Find git working trees under a set of root directories.

A root that is itself a working tree is returned directly; otherwise its
immediate subdirectories are the working trees. Nothing deeper is looked at,
which keeps the scan quick and predictable: a repository is either the root
you named or something sitting directly in it.

A root written ``user@host:path`` is looked at on that machine instead, in
one round trip rather than one per directory. The connection to each host is
opened first, so that whatever ssh asks for is asked once, before the scan
starts printing.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**roots**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Iterable](`typing.Iterable`)\[[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`crossrepo.location.Location`), [str](`str`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`)\]\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Directories to search. ``~`` is expanded, here for a local root and on the far side for a remote one. A root that does not exist, or that cannot be read, and a host that does not answer, are skipped with a [](`crossrepo.config.SourceWarning`), since there is nothing about an empty result to say which source was the problem.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[List](`typing.List`)\[[Location](`crossrepo.location.Location`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The working trees found, without duplicates, local ones as resolved paths.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
discover_repos(["~/github-backup/munch-group", "kmt@genome.au.dk:~/projects"])
```
